forces.title: Agentic AI threatens consumer credit card economics
forces.description: Agentic artificial intelligence is expected to compress consumer credit card economics. This will occur through payment rail substitution, automated repayment optimization, fee avoidance, and real-time foreign-exchange routing. The McKinsey report suggests global consumer credit card revenues face a potential $10 billion risk by 2030, with a possible disruption of 30% of net interchange in card-heavy markets. This poses a significant challenge for non-bank financial institutions involved in consumer finance.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Nonbank lenders increase competition for client wallet share
forces.description: Nonbank lenders and alternative platforms are increasingly competing with traditional banks for wallet share from global corporations, institutional investors, and financial sponsors. These challengers are seizing opportunities in the 12-25% of annual banking wallet share that rotates across clients. Financial sponsors, in particular, are leveraging alternative lenders for complex financing structures like NAV credit facilities, indicating a structural shift in how financial services are sourced and delivered.

forces.title: Client wallet share highly contestable across financial segments
forces.description: Banking relationships are no longer considered evergreen, with a significant portion of client wallet share becoming contestable annually. Corporates reallocate 12-13%, institutional investors 17%, and financial sponsors up to 25% of their wallet share each year. This ongoing re-evaluation creates a meaningful opening for challengers, including nonbank financial institutions and diversified financial conglomerates, to gain market share by proving their competitive advantages in performance, innovation, and service delivery.

forces.title: Clients prioritize execution certainty and relationships over price
forces.description: When selecting financing and lending providers, clients increasingly prioritize execution certainty, historical relationship strength, and sector expertise alongside competitive pricing. For non-bank financial institutions, this means competitive advantage stems more from reliable delivery, transparent processes, and proactive advisory rather than product features or price alone. Building trust-based relationships and demonstrating a strong track record in complex structures are critical for securing mandates from financial sponsors and institutional investors.

forces.title: Agent-directed routing demands multi-rail payment enablement
forces.description: The emergence of autonomous software agents will lead to dynamic transaction routing based on cost, speed, and trust across various payment rails. This shift will give a competitive edge to players capable of enabling agent-directed routing in multi-rail environments. Non-bank financial institutions involved in consumer finance must build positions in this "trust layer" by developing verifiable machine credentials and dynamic consent standards, as the infrastructure battle is occurring now.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Western Europe's card resilience maintains traditional payment perimeter against disruptors
viewpoints.description: McKinsey views Western Europe as a "card-resilient" market, indicating high adoption and retention of credit and debit card infrastructure through 2035. This resilience is attributed to entrenched merchant acceptance, valuable consumer rewards, and robust dispute resolution mechanisms. This stability helps preserve the traditional card perimeter, suggesting that even autonomous software agents are likely to route transactions via established card rails, rather than bypassing them for newer A2A or stablecoin networks. This is a cautiously positive outlook for consumer finance providers relying on card economics.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world
